subproblems.title: The radial test field φ(|x − y|/τ)(x − y) is C¹ with support in the closed ball of radius Aτ
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, y ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P, Euclidean norm |·|), A, τ ∈ ℝ with τ > 0, and let φ : ℝ → ℝ be a C¹ function with φ(u) = 1 for every u ≤ 1 and φ(u) = 0 for every u ≥ A. Define X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P by X(x) := φ(|x − y|/τ)·(x − y). Then (i) X is C¹ on ℝ^P (ContDiff ℝ 1 X), (ii) X has compact support, and (iii) its topological support tsupport X = closure{x : X(x) ≠ 0} is contained in the closed ball B̄_{Aτ}(y) = {x : |x − y| ≤ Aτ}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (y : Euclid P) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (A τ : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → (∀ u, u ≤ 1 → φ u = 1) → (∀ u, A ≤ u → φ u = 0) → 0 < τ → ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x : Euclid P => φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) • (x - y)) ∧ HasCompactSupport (fun x : Euclid P => φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) • (x - y)) ∧ tsupport (fun x : Euclid P => φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) • (x - y)) ⊆ closedBall y (A * τ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the radial test field X(x) = φ(r/τ)(x − y), Simon Ch. 4, 3.2–3.3 with the cutoff γ(r) = φ(r/τ)).
Notation: r(x) := |x − y| (Euclidean norm of ℝ^P), X(x) := φ(r(x)/τ)·(x − y), K := B̄_{Aτ}(y) = {x : |x − y| ≤ Aτ}, B(y, τ) := {x : |x − y| < τ}.
1. (Support.) Let x ∈ ℝ^P with X(x) ≠ 0; then φ(r(x)/τ) ≠ 0. Suppose x ∉ K, i.e. r(x) > Aτ. Since τ > 0, r(x)/τ > A, so A ≤ r(x)/τ and the hypothesis gives φ(r(x)/τ) = 0, a contradiction. Hence {x : X(x) ≠ 0} ⊆ K. The closed ball K is a closed set (isClosed_closedBall), so the closure of {X ≠ 0}, which is tsupport X, is contained in K (closure_minimal). This proves (iii).
2. (Compact support.) ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional normed space, hence proper, so the closed ball K is compact (isCompact_closedBall). tsupport X is closed (isClosed_tsupport) and, by step 1, contained in K; a closed subset of a compact set is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). Hence tsupport X is compact, i.e. X has compact support. This proves (ii).
3. (C¹ at the centre y.) Let z ∈ B(y, τ). Then r(z) < τ, so r(z)/τ < 1 because τ > 0; in particular r(z)/τ ≤ 1 and the hypothesis gives φ(r(z)/τ) = 1, so X(z) = 1·(z − y) = z − y. Since B(y, τ) is an open neighbourhood of y (τ > 0), X agrees on a neighbourhood of y with the affine map z ↦ z − y, which is C^∞ (identity minus a constant). A function that agrees on a neighbourhood of a point with a function that is C¹ at that point is itself C¹ at that point (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence X is C¹ at y.
4. (C¹ at a point x ≠ y.) Let x ≠ y. The map z ↦ z − y is C^∞ and its value at x is x − y ≠ 0. The Euclidean norm of the inner-product space ℝ^P is C^∞ at every nonzero vector (it is the square root of the C^∞ function |·|², which is positive there; Mathlib contDiffAt_norm), so by composition z ↦ r(z) = |z − y| is C^∞, in particular C¹, at x (ContDiffAt.norm). Division by the constant τ preserves this (ContDiffAt.div_const), and composing with the C¹ function φ gives that z ↦ φ(r(z)/τ) is C¹ at x (ContDiff.contDiffAt and ContDiffAt.comp). Finally X is the product (scalar times vector) of this C¹ scalar function with the C^∞ vector function z ↦ z − y, so X is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.smul).
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 4, X is C¹ at every point of ℝ^P, so X is C¹ on ℝ^P (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). This proves (i); (ii) and (iii) were proved in steps 2 and 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: If X(x) ≠ 0 then φ(|x − y|/τ) ≠ 0, so |x − y|/τ < A and |x − y| < Aτ; the closed ball is closed, so tsupport X ⊆ B̄_{Aτ}(y).
B̄_{Aτ}(y) is compact in ℝ^P, so the closed set tsupport X is compact.
On B(y, τ), |z − y|/τ < 1, so φ(|z − y|/τ) = 1 and X(z) = z − y; hence X is C¹ at y.
At x ≠ y the norm is smooth at x − y ≠ 0, so z ↦ φ(|z − y|/τ)(z − y) is C¹ at x by composition and product rules.
C¹ at every point gives ContDiff ℝ 1 X.

subproblems.title: Tangential divergence of the radial test field relative to a subspace (Simon Ch. 4, 3.2)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with orthogonal projection p := Q.starProjection : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, let y, x ∈ ℝ^P, τ ∈ ℝ with τ > 0, and let φ : ℝ → ℝ be a C¹ function with φ(u) = 1 for every u ≤ 1. Write φ' := deriv φ, X(z) := φ(|z − y|/τ)·(z − y) and DX(x) := fderiv ℝ X x. Then trace(p ∘ DX(x)) = (dim Q)·φ(|x − y|/τ) + (|x − y|/τ)·φ'(|x − y|/τ)·(1 − |(x − y) − p(x − y)|²/|x − y|²), with Lean's convention a/0 = 0 (at x = y the second summand vanishes since |x − y|/τ = 0). Here trace is the trace of a linear endomorphism of ℝ^P and dim Q = Module.finrank ℝ Q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (y x : Euclid P) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (τ : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → (∀ u, u ≤ 1 → φ u = 1) → 0 < τ → LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (Q.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ (fderiv ℝ (fun z : Euclid P => φ (‖z - y‖ / τ) • (z - y)) x).toLinearMap) = (Module.finrank ℝ Q : ℝ) * φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) + ‖x - y‖ / τ * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * (1 - ‖(x - y) - Q.starProjection (x - y)‖ ^ 2 / ‖x - y‖ ^ 2)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 (trace p_x = dim T_xM) and 6 (divergence formula for the radial field, Simon Ch. 4, 3.2) of the parent proof, with the subspace Q in place of T_xM and dim Q in place of n.
Notation: p := Q.starProjection (the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto Q, an endomorphism of ℝ^P), d := dim Q, v := x − y, r := |v|, X(z) := φ(|z − y|/τ)·(z − y), DX(x) := fderiv ℝ X x, φ' := deriv φ, I := identity of ℝ^P, ⟨·,·⟩ the Euclidean inner product.
1. (Trace of p.) For every w ∈ ℝ^P, p(w) ∈ Q (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem), and p(w) = w for every w ∈ Q (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff). Hence p is a linear projection onto Q (LinearMap.IsProj Q p): with respect to the decomposition ℝ^P = Q ⊕ ker p it is id_Q ⊕ 0. Its trace is therefore dim Q (LinearMap.IsProj.trace; Q and ker p are finite-dimensional real vector spaces, hence free and finite). So trace p = d. (Equivalently: p = ι∘π with π the orthogonal projection onto Q and ι the inclusion, and trace(ι∘π) = trace(π∘ι) = trace(id_Q) = d by LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'.)
2. (Case x = y.) For z in the open ball B(y, τ) we have |z − y|/τ < 1 (τ > 0), so φ(|z − y|/τ) = 1 and X(z) = z − y. Thus X coincides with z ↦ z − y on a neighbourhood of y, so the two maps have the same derivative at y (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), namely DX(y) = I (the derivative of the identity minus a constant). Hence trace(p ∘ DX(y)) = trace p = d by step 1. On the right-hand side, |y − y| = 0, so |y − y|/τ = 0, φ(0) = 1 (since 0 ≤ 1), and the second summand contains the factor 0; the right-hand side equals d·1 + 0 = d. The identity holds at x = y.
3. (Case x ≠ y: derivative of the radius.) Now v ≠ 0 and r > 0. The function g(z) := |z − y|² has derivative h ↦ 2⟨v, h⟩ at x (derivative of the squared norm, HasFDerivAt.norm_sq, composed with z ↦ z − y whose derivative is I). Since g(x) = r² ≠ 0, the chain rule for the square root (HasFDerivAt.sqrt) shows that z ↦ √(g(z)) has derivative h ↦ (1/(2√(r²)))·2⟨v, h⟩ at x. As √(|z − y|²) = |z − y| for every z and √(r²) = r, the map z ↦ |z − y| has derivative h ↦ r⁻¹⟨v, h⟩ at x.
4. (Derivative of X at x ≠ y.) Multiplying by the constant τ⁻¹, z ↦ |z − y|/τ has derivative h ↦ τ⁻¹r⁻¹⟨v, h⟩ at x (HasFDerivAt.mul_const). Since φ is C¹, it is differentiable at r/τ with derivative φ'(r/τ); by the chain rule (HasDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivAt), c(z) := φ(|z − y|/τ) has derivative ℓ at x, where ℓ(h) := b⟨v, h⟩ and b := φ'(r/τ)·τ⁻¹·r⁻¹. By the product rule for a scalar function times a vector function (HasFDerivAt.smul), using that z ↦ z − y has derivative I and value v at x, X has derivative DX(x)h = c(x)·h + ℓ(h)·v = a·h + b⟨v, h⟩·v at x, where a := φ(r/τ). That is, DX(x) = a·I + (h ↦ ℓ(h)·v).
5. (Trace at x ≠ y.) Composing with p gives p ∘ DX(x) = a·p + (h ↦ ℓ(h)·p(v)). The trace is linear, and for a linear functional ℓ and a vector w the rank-one map h ↦ ℓ(h)·w has trace ℓ(w) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight). With step 1, trace(p ∘ DX(x)) = a·d + ℓ(p v) = d·φ(r/τ) + b·⟨v, p v⟩.
6. (Pythagoras.) The vector v − p v is orthogonal to Q and p v ∈ Q, so ⟨v − p v, p v⟩ = 0 (Submodule.starProjection_inner_eq_zero). Hence ⟨v, p v⟩ = ⟨p v, p v⟩ = |p v|². Expanding the square, |v − p v|² = |v|² − 2⟨v, p v⟩ + |p v|² = r² − ⟨v, p v⟩ (norm_sub_sq_real). Therefore ⟨v, p v⟩ = r² − |v − p v|².
7. (Algebra.) Since r ≠ 0, b·⟨v, p v⟩ = φ'(r/τ)·τ⁻¹·r⁻¹·(r² − |v − p v|²) = (r/τ)·φ'(r/τ)·(1 − |v − p v|²/r²). Substituting into step 5, trace(p ∘ DX(x)) = d·φ(r/τ) + (r/τ)·φ'(r/τ)·(1 − |(x − y) − p(x − y)|²/|x − y|²), which is the claim at x ≠ y. Steps 2 and 7 cover all x. ∎
proof_key_steps: p = Q.starProjection is a projection onto Q, so trace p = dim Q (LinearMap.IsProj.trace).
x = y: X(z) = z − y on B(y, τ), so DX(y) = I and both sides equal dim Q (φ(0) = 1, |y − y|/τ = 0).
x ≠ y: z ↦ |z − y| has derivative r⁻¹⟨v, ·⟩ (square-root chain rule), so DX(x) = φ(r/τ)I + φ'(r/τ)τ⁻¹r⁻¹⟨v, ·⟩v.
trace(p ∘ DX(x)) = dim Q·φ(r/τ) + φ'(r/τ)τ⁻¹r⁻¹⟨v, pv⟩ by linearity and the rank-one trace formula.
⟨v, pv⟩ = r² − |v − pv|² by orthogonality of v − pv and pv; algebra with r ≠ 0 gives the formula.

subproblems.title: First variation as a weight integral, with integrable tangential divergence (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with weight μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), and X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a C¹ vector field with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U. Assume x ↦ p_x is μ-AEMeasurable, where p_x is the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x. Then x ↦ div_M X(x) := tangentialDivergence n M X x = trace(p_x ∘ DX(x)) is μ-integrable and R.firstVariation X (= ∫_M θ·div_M X dHⁿ) equals ∫ div_M X dμ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (X : Euclid P → Euclid P), ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ U → AEMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) R.measure → Integrable (fun x => tangentialDivergence n R.carrier X x) R.measure ∧ R.firstVariation X = ∫ x, tangentialDivergence n R.carrier X x ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dsmc_firstVariation_eq_integral (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.mean_curvature_monotonicity-a1.first_variation_integral-a1, status accepted, candidate 6c199bd2f71cf6454e96792be486679e1ca03ac1), proposed under the same bare name with its byte-identical frozen type and reused here. It supplies step 4 ((P4)) of the parent proof and the integrability of div_M X used in step 7. Its proof is recorded below.
Source: Simon Ch. 4, 2.2 (δV(X) = ∫ div_M X dμ_V) and 4.1.1 (μ_V = θHⁿ⌞M).
Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, Hⁿ := μHE[n], ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M, μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity (x ↦ (θ(x) : [0, ∞])); p_x := (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection; K := tsupport X, compact with K ⊆ U; D(x) := fderiv ℝ X x; div(x) := tangentialDivergence n M X x = trace(p_x ∘ D(x)).
1. (Measurability.) Let tr : L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) → ℝ be the trace; it is a linear functional on a finite-dimensional normed space, hence a continuous linear map, and div(x) = tr(p_x ∘ D(x)) by definition. The composition map (q, E) ↦ q ∘ E is a continuous bilinear map on L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) × L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) (isBoundedBilinearMap_comp). D is continuous because X is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable; x ↦ p_x is μ-AEMeasurable by hypothesis, hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable (the finite-dimensional space L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) is second countable and metrizable). A continuous function of two μ-a.e. strongly measurable maps is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂), so div is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
2. (Bound.) An orthogonal projection has operator norm at most 1 (Submodule.starProjection_norm_le), so |div(x)| ≤ ‖tr‖·‖p_x ∘ D(x)‖ ≤ ‖tr‖·‖p_x‖·‖D(x)‖ ≤ ‖tr‖·‖D(x)‖. X vanishes on the open complement of K, so D(x) = 0 and div(x) = 0 for x ∉ K (fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport). D is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), hence bounded: ‖D(x)‖ ≤ C for some C and all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Hence |div(x)| ≤ 1_K(x)·‖tr‖·C for every x.
3. (Integrability.) K is compact, hence closed and Borel measurable, and K ⊆ U. By withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict, μ(K) = ∫_K θ dν = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ, which is finite by the field R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to K. Hence the indicator 1_K·‖tr‖·C is μ-integrable (integrableOn_const on a set of finite measure, integrable_indicator_iff), and div, which is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (step 1) and dominated by it everywhere (step 2), is μ-integrable (Integrable.mono').
4. (Identity.) θ is measurable (R.measurable_mult composed with the cast ℕ → [0, ∞], measurable as a map out of ℕ) and every value (θ(x) : [0, ∞]) is finite. The density formula for Bochner integrals, ∫ g d(ν.withDensity f) = ∫ f(x).toReal·g(x) dν(x) for measurable a.e.-finite f and every g (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul), gives ∫ div dμ = ∫ (θ(x) : [0, ∞]).toReal·div(x) dν(x) = ∫_M θ(x)·tangentialDivergence n M X x dHⁿ(x), using (θ(x) : [0, ∞]).toReal = θ(x). The last integral is R.firstVariation X by definition (IMRep.firstVariation). Together with step 3 this proves both conclusions. ∎
proof_key_steps: div_M X(x) = tr(p_x ∘ DX(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (continuous trace and composition, continuous DX, a.e.-measurable p_x).
|div_M X| ≤ ‖tr‖·sup‖DX‖·1_{tsupport X}, since ‖p_x‖ ≤ 1 and DX = 0 off tsupport X.

subproblems.title: The approximate tangent planes are n-dimensional for μ-almost every point (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with weight μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for μ-almost every x ∈ ℝ^P the subspace T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x (the chosen approximate tangent plane when one exists, the zero subspace otherwise) has dimension n: Module.finrank ℝ (approxTangentPlane n M x) = n.

This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dorag_aa_ae_finrank_approxTangentPlane (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.allard_graph-a1.affine_approximation-a1.tangent_dimension-a1, status accepted, candidate db9124843c506359873f91062030c510610c3800), proposed under the same bare name with its byte-identical frozen type and reused here. It supplies the dimension statement of step 5 ((P3)) of the parent proof. Its proof is recorded below.
Source: IMRep.orients (Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1) and the definition of approxTangentPlane (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4).
Notation: M := R.carrier, ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M, μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ.
1. (The dimension is part of the tangent predicate.) In SimonGMT Chapter03, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q includes the condition Module.finrank ℝ Q = n, available as the accessor HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.finrank_eq.
2. (Pointwise consequence.) Fix x for which some subspace Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, and let h be the statement ∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. By the frozen definition, approxTangentPlane n M x is 'if h then h.choose else ⊥'; since h holds, approxTangentPlane n M x = h.choose (dite_eq_left). The chosen subspace satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x h.choose (Exists.choose_spec), so by step 1, Module.finrank ℝ (approxTangentPlane n M x) = n.
3. (Existence ν-a.e.) The field R.orients states that for ν-almost every x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q. Discarding the second conjunct, E(x) :≡ ∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q holds for ν-a.e. x.
4. (Transfer to μ.) μ = ν.withDensity θ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so every ν-null set is μ-null (Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le); hence E(x) holds for μ-a.e. x.
5. (Conclusion.) By step 2, Module.finrank ℝ (approxTangentPlane n M x) = n at every x with E(x), and by step 4 this is μ-almost every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q includes finrank Q = n.
Where an approximate tangent plane exists, approxTangentPlane n M x is the chosen one, so its finrank is n.
R.orients gives existence for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x.
μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M transfers this to μ-a.e. x.

subproblems.title: Compact subsets of U have finite weight (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n): M = R.carrier is Borel with M ⊆ U, θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M, and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Let μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Then for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U: Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ and μ(K) < ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ K) ≠ ∞ ∧ R.measure K ≠ ∞

This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.imrep_local_finiteness-a1, status accepted, candidate 702e7082a5a7012f7a8f6efd9d272697e426f50b), proposed under the same bare name with its byte-identical frozen type and reused here. It supplies μ(B̄_{Aτ}(y)) < ∞ in step 7 ((P2)) of the parent proof. Its proof is recorded below.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (θ is a locally Hⁿ-integrable positive integer-valued function), encoded by the IMRep fields mult_pos and locallyIntegrable_mult.
Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], M = R.carrier, θ(x) = R.mult x ∈ ℕ ⊆ [0, ∞], μ = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U.
1. K is a compact subset of the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, hence Borel (IsCompact.measurableSet).
2. (Weight of K.) Since K is measurable, μ(K) = ∫_K θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) by the definition of withDensity (withDensity_apply), and (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ after commuting the intersection.
3. The field locallyIntegrable_mult, applied to the compact set K ⊆ U, gives ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞; by step 2, μ(K) ≠ ∞. This is the second conclusion.
4. (θ ≥ 1 on M.) For x ∈ M ∩ K the field mult_pos gives 0 < R.mult x in ℕ, hence 1 ≤ R.mult x, and after the cast to [0, ∞], 1 ≤ θ(x).
5. (Measurability.) θ is measurable: it is the composition of the measurable map R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ (field measurable_mult) with the cast ℕ → [0, ∞], and every map out of the discrete space ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat).
6. (Unweighted measure.) Hⁿ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dHⁿ (setLIntegral_one) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ by monotonicity of the set lower integral (setLIntegral_mono) with steps 4 and 5; the right side is finite by step 3, so Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞. This is the first conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact K is closed, hence Borel.
μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ by withDensity_apply and restrict_restrict.
locallyIntegrable_mult makes this finite.
